entities.summary:
Ezekiel the Tragedian was an Egyptian actor who wrote in Alexandria. Born in Egypt during the Hellenistic period, Ezekiel the Tragedian is best known for his works in Greek tragedy. Naomi Yavneh dated his work to the 3rd century BCE, while Howard Jacobson estimates the 2nd century BCE. Evidence of the date is not definitive.

Ezekiel the Tragedian's primary works were written during the reign of Ptolemy III, who ruled Egypt from 246 to 221 BCE. His works were likely influenced by the Alexandrian Museum, a major center of Greek learning and culture. Ezekiel the Tragedian's writing style was characterized by its use of rhetorical devices and poetic language.

The legacy of Ezekiel the Tragedian can be seen in the works of later Greek tragedians, such as Sophocles and Euripides. His influence also extended to the development of Western drama, with many of his works being studied and performed for centuries.

In conclusion, Ezekiel the Tragedian's significance lies in his contributions to the development of Greek tragedy and his enduring influence on Western drama.

Ezekiel the Tragedian was a key figure in the cultural and literary landscape of ancient Alexandria, leaving behind a lasting legacy that continues to be felt today.
